correctness.rationale: For every real invertible 2-by-2 A with singular values a>=b>0 and 0<tau<b, SVD invariance and Gaussian polar independence yield T~chi-square(2), U~Beta(1/2,1/2), and ||Ag1||^2=T d(U). A perpendicular row calculation gives exact rank-one Frobenius residual squared a^2 b^2/d(U). Conditional on g1, the next Gaussian test norm is R|Z|, so multiplying its erf probability by the conditional first-gate pass factor and integrating over U proves p0 and p1 without falsely assuming independent gates. Change of variable gives the CDF/density including the a=b case; dominated convergence gives the positive high-condition-number limit. Eckart-Young enforces error>=b for rank <=1. Explicit verifier independently tested 400000 direct sequential Gaussian cases, 100000 residual-law samples, elementary endpoint identities and asymptotic quadrature consistency. Numerical tests supplement the exact proof; no unproved infinite extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: Adaptive fixed-tolerance low-rank approximation is designed to meet a target error while estimating rank from cheap residual probes. The complete achievable rank-decision law for the smallest nontrivial full-rank model gives the actual failure rate across arbitrary spectral ratios, not just mean unbiasedness or an isolated negative instance. The strict below-best-rank-one regime exposes a quantitative 24.7% asymptotic false-stop floor for half-minimum-singular-value tolerance; the first-gate/rank-update coupling makes this a meaningful design-risk calculation for single-probe stopping. It motivates calibrated or repeated validation even for very anisotropic matrices. Scope remains intentionally limited to the rigorously analyzed small-dimensional stochastic mechanism.
